Brothers, if you’ve been in the crypto market for more than 2 years, you should all know that the essence of trading is a battle between the market and your own impulses.
In the past, I always thought that not being able to make money meant I lacked a set of “holy grail” methods. In the end, I realized that what truly wrecks an account is having no rules and just messing around.

The core lesson from 10 years of trading pitfalls #ETH 
I’ve been in the market for 10 years. The path from 10,000 to 100,000—my biggest loss was trusting the “me right now” too much:
When the price rises, I’d be convinced it can keep going higher. I’d blindly chase high-priced orders—while floating losses piled up, I’d think, “I’ll average down and lower the cost.” The more I averaged down, the heavier the position got. Just after I made a bit of profit, I’d assume the next trade could replicate the same gains. I opened positions frequently.
I put a “tightening spell” on my trading impulses #zec 

Later, I completely cut out the extra room for me to act impulsively, and locked my urges down with rules:
Manage the principal by splitting it. Only keep a small portion as trading capital. In the beginning, only trade low-risk spot. Put leverage trades aside until the trading system is mature. Also, predefine the number of averaging-down attempts—once those times are used up, even if you’re still in floating loss, you absolutely don’t add more. When your profit reaches the preset target, withdraw a portion immediately to secure gains. Strictly limit how often you monitor the market and place orders. No more staring at charts for ten-plus hours, afraid of missing opportunities #pumpbtc 

After doing it for a long time, I finally understood: the most dangerous thing in the market is never that you don’t have opportunities, but that you mistakenly believe every fluctuation is a chance to make money. Long-term stable profitability has never depended on being right with a big bet on a single occasion. More often, it’s because when you want to rush in, you manage to hold back; when you want to average down, you stop; and when you make money, you take profits in time. In the end, trading isn’t really competing with the market—it’s a long practice of spending time battling your own impulses. Full-time crypto trading, contracts养家 @Square-Creator-e6126298997b7

I hear a lot of people saying that $UNI  has really been grinding people down recently.
Every day it just hovers around the 9-dollar mark—can’t really move up, and when it drops it doesn’t fall deep.
Most people seeing this kind of trend probably start getting annoyed: 
“Is UNI done for?”

But I actually think this stage is the easiest time to shake people out.
Look at the trading volume before—then you’ll understand.
When $UNI  surged on September 23, the single-day trading volume briefly exceeded $1.4 billion. After that, as the price pulled back, the volume clearly cooled off too.

This is actually pretty normal.
The people who chased in earlier are rotating their positions; short-term capital is withdrawing, and the market begins to find a new balance.
What’s truly worth watching, though, is whether around the $9 level there’s ongoing panic selling.
From what I’m seeing right now, it feels more like this: it can’t go up, but nobody seems willing to dump aggressively.

This kind of market is definitely boring.
But it’s also often the place where people regret it the most.
And don’t forget: CME plans to launch UNI futures on October 19, and it’s still pending regulatory review.
So my stance on UNI is simple right now: I’m not worried about going sideways—I’d rather add more if it drops.

Because real big moves never come with a notice telling you in advance:
“Brothers, I’m starting the pump tomorrow.”
It usually happens right when everyone thinks it’s boring and has no point—then suddenly volume spikes.

And by then, if UNI breaks through the previous high again, you’ll probably see another wave of people come out asking:
“Can $UNI  still be chased?”
I’d rather think through the position and the logic before nobody’s talking about it.
The longer it grinds around $9, the more I want to know which direction it’s ultimately preparing to move.
Don’t wait until it starts moving—you only begin to FOMO.👀

听到很多人说，$UNI 最近是真的磨人。
每天就在9刀附近晃来晃去，涨也涨不动，跌也跌不深。

这其实很正常。
前面追进去的人在换手，短线资金退潮，市场开始重新找平衡。
真正值得看的，反而是9刀附近到底有没有持续出现恐慌性抛售。
目前我看到的感觉更像是：涨不动，但也没人愿意疯狂砸。

这种盘面确实最无聊。
但也往往是最容易让人后悔的位置。
而且别忘了，CME计划10月19日推出UNI期货，目前仍待监管审查。
所以我现在对UNI的态度很简单：横盘我不慌，跌下来我更想加仓。

因为真正的大行情从来不会提前告诉你：
“兄弟们，我明天开始拉盘了。”
它往往就是在所有人觉得无聊、觉得没意思的时候，突然放量。

到时候如果UNI重新突破前高，估计又会有一群人跑出来问：

我反而更想在没人讨论的时候，把位置和逻辑先想清楚。

以太坊ETH市场深度分析：杠杆ETP获批后的机遇与挑战

一、价格走势回顾

北京时间2026年10月5日凌晨，以太坊报价2702美元，过去24小时内最高触及2738美元，涨幅约0.89%。从小时K线来看，ETH在触及2733美元布林带上轨附近后遭遇明显阻力，随后连续四根小时阴线将价格从2731美元拉低至2698美元，目前在2700美元整数关口附近企稳。现货交易量方面，最近一小时成交量约3027万美元，较前一小时有所萎缩，显示市场在关键位置观望情绪浓厚。本轮行情的主要催化剂是SEC批准了首批以太坊杠杆ETP产品，包括三倍做多和三倍做空的以太坊期货ETF，这为传统投资者提供了更丰富的风险敞口工具。

二、技术指标解读

均线系统显示，当前价格已跌破7周期均线2719美元，但仍维持在25周期均线2707美元和99周期均线2699美元上方，三线呈多头排列但间距收窄，暗示上行动能正在减弱。布林带方面，上轨2733美元恰好是本轮高点位置，中轨2709美元，下轨2684美元，价格从上轨回落至中轨附近，短期波动区间收窄至约50美元。

MACD指标出现高位死叉迹象，DIFF线从9.08回落至5.27，DEA线维持在6.44附近，MACD柱状图由正转负至负1.17，虽然空头信号尚不强烈，但动能衰减趋势明确。RSI指标快速降温，6周期RSI从74.0回落至35.5，12周期RSI从71.6回落至45.6，已经接近中性区域，说明短期超买状态已基本释放。KDJ指标方面，K值降至34.1，D值降至51.7，J值跌至负1.27，接近超卖区域，短线可能出现技术性反弹。

抛物线SAR指标翻转至2738美元位于价格上方，形成短期空头信号。SuperTrend指标维持在2701美元，当前价格刚好位于其上方，这是关键的多空分界线。如果价格有效跌破2700美元SuperTrend支撑，可能触发更大级别的回调。ATR指标显示14周期平均真实波幅为10.85美元，波动率处于正常水平，未出现极端波动。

三、市场情绪分析

💼💼💼 Macro & Geopolitics Board: "Pretext" to legitimize the price route

​Financial markets never move randomly; news is the tool Market Makers (MM) use to legitimize liquidity sweeps:
​Monetary Policy & Inflation: Expectations that the Fed will keep easing rates after weaker employment data. When the market consensus is that "cheap money is about to return," retail will tend to go All-in Long with high leverage.

​Geopolitical tensions: Escalating instability in the Middle East or military/trade deterrence moves are always used as an "FUD trigger" to create sudden red candles (flash crashes) to shake out weak-hand positions.

​"Uptober" trap psychology: October, historically, is always a strong growth month for Crypto (Uptober). MM knows the crowd is waiting to buy and expects a Q4 breakout—creating the most favorable conditions to set a liquidity trap.

​#BTC #ETH #SmartMoney #Onchain  #LiquidationAlert

Date: 5 October 2026  
Market view: Bullish / confirmation-sensitive  
Primary timeframe: 7-day daily closes, with live snapshot for the current session
Why this coin deserves attention today
$ETH  is pressing higher again, and the structure is improving without yet looking euphoric. The interesting part of today's setup is not simply the percentage move. It is the relationship between the current live price, the recent closing range, liquidity and the broader market regime.
ETH is not as stretched as several altcoins. Its five-period RSI is around the low 60s, leaving more room for a continuation attempt if the recent high is reclaimed.
Whether eth can turn a recovery into a sustained trend is the core trading question. This is not a call that price must move in one direction; it is a framework for deciding which confirmation would make the setup stronger and which level would invalidate it.
Market snapshot
Data note: The live snapshot comes from CoinMarketCap's current market page. The technical chart uses CoinMarketCap daily USDT closes recorded at 00:00 UTC. Because crypto trades continuously, a live price and a daily close will not always match exactly.
Market structure
The seven-day closing range is $2,669 to $2,727. The closing-window change is +1.47%. The 3-period EMA calculated from those closes is $2,712.
Current price is above that short EMA. That is useful as a short-term trend filter, but it should not be treated as a standalone signal.
The market is best described as bullish on this short window. The most important question is whether buyers can establish acceptance above the recent high rather than briefly trading through it. Conversely, a loss of the recent low would change the short-term structure from recovery/continuation into a deeper retracement.
Technical analysis
Momentum
The 5-period RSI calculated from the seven daily closes is 62.7. That reading suggests positive but not extreme momentum.
RSI is a momentum measure, not a timing guarantee. In strong trends it can remain elevated for longer than expected; in falling markets it can remain weak even after a bounce begins.
Range and EMA
Price is interacting with a clearly defined recent range. The 3-EMA at $2,712 provides a simple dynamic reference: holding above it supports continuation, while repeated closes below it would suggest momentum is fading.
Volume and liquidity
24-hour turnover is approximately 2.98% of market capitalization. That is a useful liquidity/participation measure, but it is not the same as order-book depth. High turnover can support a breakout, yet it can also accelerate liquidation when positioning is crowded.
Key levels
These levels are derived from the seven daily closes, not guaranteed targets:
- Support zone: $2,669 — the lowest close in the window.
- Resistance zone: $2,727 — the highest close in the window.
- Breakout confirmation: sustained trade/close above roughly $2,754.
- Invalidation reference: below roughly $2,642.
- Potential target zone 1: around $2,756 if the breakout holds.
- Potential target zone 2: around $2,785 in a stronger range-expansion scenario.
The target zones are mechanical extensions of the observed range, not predictions. A trader should reassess them if market structure changes.
Fundamental / ecosystem context
Ethereum remains the largest general-purpose smart-contract settlement layer, with a large DeFi and application ecosystem.
Barron's reports Ethereum gained more than 70% in Q3 2026. The broader institutional backdrop is also improving as the SEC has proposed a crypto-custody framework for registered investment advisers.
For this article, the fundamental case is intentionally separated from the technical setup. A strong project does not guarantee a strong token trade, and a strong chart does not prove improving fundamentals.
Catalysts to watch
1. Price acceptance: Can the market close beyond the current resistance area rather than only wick through it?
2. Volume confirmation: Does turnover expand with the breakout, or does price rise while liquidity thins?
3. Bitcoin regime: Large-cap altcoins remain sensitive to BTC direction and broader risk appetite.
4. Coin-specific development: Barron's reports Ethereum gained more than 70% in Q3 2026. The broader institutional backdrop is also improving as the SEC has proposed a crypto-custody framework for registered investment advisers.
Bear case
ETH still trades materially below its 2025 all-time high, so the recovery remains vulnerable to macro risk-off moves and rejection near recent highs. A second bearish path is a broader crypto reversal. If Bitcoin loses its current recovery structure, high-beta assets can underperform even when their individual charts initially look constructive.
The most important warning sign is therefore not a single red candle. It is a sequence of lower highs and lower lows accompanied by failed attempts to reclaim the recent range.
Bull case
The bullish case becomes stronger if price holds above the 3-EMA, breaks the recent high, and then turns that former resistance into support. A breakout accompanied by strong liquidity would be more convincing than a thin-volume spike.
For the most aggressive momentum names, the bull case also requires accepting that volatility can expand dramatically. Confirmation matters more than prediction.
Trader scenarios
🟢 Bullish scenario: Price closes above $2,754, volume remains healthy, and the former resistance begins acting as support. The range-extension zones become the next areas to monitor.
🟡 Neutral scenario: Price remains between $2,669 and $2,727. Range trading may dominate, with false breakouts possible.
🔴 Bearish scenario: Price loses $2,642 and fails to reclaim the range floor. That would invalidate the current continuation/recovery thesis and shift attention to lower support.
Risk management
This is market analysis, not financial advice. Position size should reflect volatility rather than conviction. A useful framework is to define the invalidation level before entry, keep risk per trade small enough that a normal crypto volatility spike is survivable, and avoid increasing size simply because price is moving quickly.
For high-turnover assets such as ETH, slippage and liquidation risk can rise sharply during fast moves. Do not treat the mechanical target zones above as guaranteed outcomes.

#ETH  The exit queue is 37,000 ETH below the morning snapshot; this should not be read as ETH already sold

The “Ethereum exit queue hits a 2026 high” headline remains at No. 3 on Binance Square’s trending list this round. What has changed is that the current reading is lower than the morning sample. At 05:40 Beijing time on October 5, the ValidatorQueue page showed 804,419 ETH in the exit queue, with a wait of 13 days and 23 hours. When checked again at 22:40, the same page showed 767,349 ETH, with a wait of 13 days and 8 hours. The page also noted that the data came from beaconcha.in and had been updated about 41 minutes earlier. Based on the page’s figures, the two readings differ by 37,070 ETH, or about 4.6%. However, the current figure is not an on-chain reading precisely timestamped at 22:40.

A more accurate description, then, is that the exit queue remains large, but this sample is lower than the morning reading. The roughly 786,000 ETH cited in the trending post is an approximation from yet another point in time. Differences in page update times, rounding, and when the figures were checked can account for the discrepancy; figures from multiple sources should not be combined into a continuous minute-by-minute curve. Compared with this account’s earlier post from 05:42 (post ID 373796727214284), the new information is a later snapshot from the same page, down from 804,419 ETH, and a 15-hour reduction in the estimated wait. This is not enough to prove that the queue will continue to decline.

It is also important to distinguish “exit” from “withdrawal” at the protocol level. Ethereum’s official guidance says validators become eligible for withdrawal only after passing through the exit queue, and their balances must then wait for a withdrawal sweep. ValidatorQueue at the time also listed a sweep delay of about 7.5 days. An exit request is not an inflow to an exchange, nor does it mean the ETH has already been sold. The total queue also cannot identify how many of its validators are related to the MetaMask incident.

The original disclosure in the Lido Research Forum on September 30 said that affected validators had begun exiting as a precaution and that exits were expected to be completed by October 7. This refers to exit processing, not to all withdrawals being completed. This review found no newer official update since then. The focus should be on subsequent updates from the same data source and announcements from Lido and MetaMask, rather than on the total queue figure alone.

#ETH Q3 gains outpaced BTC, but order-book depth tells a different story

The No. 2 topic on Binance Square’s trending list this time put two claims side by side: “ETH rose about 70% in Q3, while liquidity declined.” First, let’s clarify the time period and definitions. Based on Binance spot daily candles, ETH/USDT rose about 70.87%, from an opening price of $1,572 on July 1 to a closing price of $2,686.01 on September 30. Over the same period, BTC/USDT rose about 42.64%, from $58,624.71 to $83,623.60. These are like-for-like calculations of quarterly price returns; they do not mean prices rose every day during the period.

“Liquidity” here refers to executable depth in the limit order book near the current price—not trading volume, on-chain TVL, or the total supply of stablecoins. CoinGecko’s 2026 CEX Depth Report, updated on September 30, says that within a narrow band of 0.15% above and below ETH’s spot price (about ±$3), the median ETH depth across eight exchanges was around $13 million to $14 million, or 35%–45% of the depth in the corresponding BTC price band. Compared with the same band in 2025, the report puts the ETH/BTC ratio at at least around 60% previously. So “declined” describes the order-book size relative to the same period last year, not a claim that “ETH liquidity fell every day in Q3.”

There is no contradiction between these figures: prices can be substantially repriced even as the buffer of orders near the market price thins relative to BTC. A depth snapshot shows how many orders are available within a given price band; it does not measure all tradable capital in the market or predict the market impact of the next large order. The report also shows that 7 of the 8 exchanges studied had more than $1 million of depth on each side of ETH’s ±$3 band. The cross-exchange median is not the same as the order book on any one platform.

Therefore, the 70% figure on the trending list can be recalculated from the quarter’s opening and closing daily candles. “Declining liquidity” should be precisely framed as the cross-exchange order-book comparison in CoinGecko’s report—not as a refutation of the price rise or as an inevitable risk signal. Going forward, it is worth tracking depth time series calculated using the same methodology, exchange coverage, and changes on the bid and ask sides. Quarter-to-quarter comparisons are valid only when definitions and samples remain consistent.

#ETH 三季度涨幅跑赢 BTC，订单簿深度却是另一回事

本轮币安广场热榜第2位把两件事并列：“ETH三季度涨约70%，流动性下降”。先拆开时间窗和定义。按Binance现货日线，ETH/USDT从7月1日开盘1572美元至9月30日收盘2686.01美元，涨幅约70.87%；BTC/USDT同期从58624.71美元至83623.60美元，约涨42.64%。这是季度价格回报的同口径计算，不代表期间每天都上涨。

“流动性”这里指限价订单簿在现价附近可成交的深度，不是成交额、链上TVL或稳定币总量。CoinGecko 9月30日更新的2026 CEX深度报告称，在ETH现价上下0.15%（约±3美元）的窄区间，ETH跨8家交易所的中位深度约1300万至1400万美元，约为BTC对应区间深度的35%–45%；报告与2025年同区间相比，ETH/BTC比例此前至少约60%。所以“下降”是相对去年同口径订单簿规模的描述，不能改写成“ETH在Q3每一天都流动性下滑”。

这组数据不矛盾：价格可以大幅重估，同时近价挂单缓冲相对BTC变薄。深度快照回答的是给定价差内有多少挂单，不是全市场可交易资金，也不能预测下一笔大单的冲击成本。报告还显示7/8家被研究交易所，在ETH±3美元区间每侧深度超过100万美元；跨所中位数与单个平台盘口也不是一回事。

因此，热榜中的70%可由季度首末日线复算；“流动性下滑”应准确限定为CoinGecko报告的跨所订单簿比较，而非价格上涨的反证或必然风险信号。后续值得看同一方法的深度时间序列、交易所覆盖和买卖两侧变化；只有定义和样本保持一致，季度间比较才成立。

ETH staking exit queue hits a new high for 2026! 786,000 ETH waiting to exit!

Ethereum has posted another noteworthy figure:
The ETH staking exit queue has climbed to its highest level so far in 2026!
Around 786,000 ETH are currently waiting to exit staking. At current prices, that’s worth more than $2 billion, with an estimated wait time of nearly 14 days.

At first glance, does that sound a little alarming?
A large amount of ETH exiting staking → could it trigger a sell-off?
But the situation this time isn’t quite that simple.

This wave of exits is mainly related to a recent security incident involving MetaMask.
MetaMask has begun proactively withdrawing some of its validators. Around 17,000 validators, representing more than 523,000 ETH, are involved in these exits.

So this doesn’t mean:
Investors are collectively dumping ETH in large numbers.

More accurately, it means:
Some validators temporarily exit → enter the exit queue → the funds may be staked again later.

And here’s an even more interesting figure:
Around 1.45 million ETH are still waiting to enter staking.

In other words:
Many want to exit, but even more want to stake.
This means the figure worth paying more attention to right now isn’t the “786,000 ETH exiting” figure itself.

It’s this:
After exiting, will this ETH enter the market, or return to the staking ecosystem?
If most of the exits are simply technical adjustments by MetaMask-related validators, the actual selling pressure on ETH may be much lower than the headline figure suggests.

On the other hand, if exits continue to grow while funds entering staking decline significantly, that’s when we should be cautious.

In short:
A record-high exit queue ≠ ETH is about to crash.
This looks more like a large-scale validator adjustment triggered by a specific event.
What really matters is where the ETH goes after exiting.

title: 📐 Grid Aritmética vs. Geométrica: Cómo elegir la distribución matemática óptima para tu Bot
subTitle:
Al configurar un Spot Grid o Futures Grid en Binance, una de las primeras decisiones técnicas es seleccionar el modo de espaciado de las órdenes: Aritmético o Geométrico. Aunque a simple vista parece un detalle secundario, la elección incorrecta puede distorsionar el porcentaje de beneficio por grilla y reducir significativamente la eficiencia de tu capital en rangos amplios.
La diferencia radica en la fórmula matemática que utiliza el bot para calcular la distancia entre cada orden de compra y venta a lo largo del canal operativo.
1. La Matemática del Espaciado: Diferencia de Fórmulas
Modo Aritmético (Paso Fijo en USDT): Cada nivel se establece a una distancia monetaria constante (ej. cada $\$100$ en $BTC$). Esto significa que el porcentaje de ganancia por grilla decrece a medida que el precio sube y aumenta cuando el precio baja.Modo Geométrico (Paso Fijo en Porcentaje): Cada nivel se establece a una distancia porcentual constante (ej. cada $0.80\%$). El diferencial de precio en USDT se expande dinámicamente a medida que el activo cotiza más alto, manteniendo el margen de beneficio neto constante en cada ciclo.
2. Cuándo Utilizar Cada Distribución
Grilla Aritmética: Ideal para rangos estrechos de consolidación y activos con baja volatilidad o precio estable. Al mantener un diferencial de precio fijo, garantiza una ejecución uniforme dentro de un canal comprimido.Grilla Geométrica: Indispensable para rangos de precios amplios (Macro Grillas), tendencias alcistas prolongadas o activos altamente volátiles. Evita que las órdenes superiores generen rendimientos porcentuales insignificantes.
3. Consejo Táctico Express (La Regla del Rango del 20%)
💡 El "Tip" Matemático: Utiliza la Grilla Aritmética únicamente cuando la diferencia entre el precio límite superior e inferior de tu bot sea menor al $20\%$. Si tu rango supera el $20\%$ de amplitud (ej. configurando $BTC$ entre $\$50,000$ y $\$80,000$), cambia obligatoriamente a Grilla Geométrica para asegurar que el beneficio de cada transacción cubra de forma constante las comisiones de la plataforma.
👉 ¿Sueles dejar la distribución por defecto o calculas si te conviene Aritmética o Geométrica según el rango? ¡Déjame tu experiencia en los comentarios!
Si este análisis cuantitativo te ayuda a optimizar tus bots en Binance, sígueme para continuar descubriendo más estrategias automatizadas.

截至2026年10月5日下午1点，以太坊现货价格报2713.8美元，过去24小时内上涨约0.44%。从小时级别K线来看，ETH在过去6小时内波动相对温和，价格区间在2709美元至2726美元之间。最近一根小时K线收于2721.5美元，显示出小幅反弹。

I recently saw CF Benchmarks’ fourth-quarter report and took another careful look at $UNI .
One figure really stood out:
They put together a basket of the 10 protocols with the highest fees from early July to September 17, and it rose 79.3%. The 10 with the lowest fees rose just 18.1%.

This suggests that a very important shift may be underway in the market:
People used to trade on narratives. Now some are starting to ask whether a project can actually make money.
And UNI is a special case.

In the past, no matter how much Uniswap’s trading volume grew or how much the protocol earned, it was hard for UNI holders to share directly in that value.
Now things are different.
Protocol fees go into TokenJar and are then used through a mechanism to $UNI  burn tokens.
In other words, the more active trading is on Uniswap, the more protocol fees it generates, and the more directly that feeds into UNI’s value-capture model.

More importantly, CF also mentioned a figure this time that I think is easy to overlook:
The average daily trading volume of on-chain U.S. stock tokens in the third quarter was 8.6 times that of the second quarter.
And a large share of this trading takes place on DEXs.

So when you look at UNI again, it’s no longer enough to simply call it “the veteran DEX leader.”
It’s now starting to combine trading volume, protocol revenue, and value capture.
Of course, the risks are clear too: if the market cools, trading volume will fall, and fee revenue will drop along with it. This cuts both ways.

But here’s the question:
If on-chain trading continues to grow in the next phase, what could UNI become?
I think that’s what’s most worth thinking about when it’s around $9.
A lot of people are still waiting to see when UNI will break out again.
I think the moments truly worth FOMOing into are often not the breakout itself, but when the market is still hesitant and the price hasn’t fully priced in future revenue.
$UNI  I’m still holding, and if it drops further, I’ll keep adding to my position.

最近看到CF Benchmarks的四季度报告，我又认真想了一遍$UNI 。

他们把7月初到9月17日手续费最高的10个协议做了个组合，涨了79.3%。手续费最低的10个，只涨了18.1%。

这说明现在市场可能正在发生一个很重要的变化：
以前大家炒的是故事，现在开始有人看你到底能不能赚钱了。
而UNI比较特殊。

以前Uniswap交易量再大，协议赚再多，UNI持有人其实很难直接分享到这部分价值。
现在不一样了。
协议费用进入TokenJar，再通过机制用于$UNI 销毁。
换句话说，Uniswap的交易越活跃，产生的协议费用越多，对UNI的价值捕获逻辑就越直接。

更关键的是，CF这次还提到一个我觉得很容易被忽略的数据：
三季度链上美股代币的日均交易量，是二季度的 8.6倍。
而这类交易很大一部分就在DEX完成。

所以你再回头看UNI，就不是简单一句“DEX老龙头”了。
它现在开始同时具备：交易量、协议收入、价值捕获。
当然，风险也很明显，市场一旦冷下来，成交量下降，手续费收入也会跟着掉，这个逻辑是双刃剑。

但问题来了：
如果下一阶段链上交易继续放大，UNI又会变成什么？
我觉得这才是现在9刀附近最值得想的东西。
很多人还在等UNI什么时候重新突破。

$UNI 我还是继续拿着，如果再跌，再继续加仓。

title: Сильный прогноз ещё не повод входить: сигнал ETH с оценкой 81,4%, который не прошёл проверку
subTitle:
Оценка сигнала — 81,4%. Направление — вверх. На первый взгляд, такой прогноз хочется сразу превратить в сделку. 5 октября в журнале моего проекта MaBuy зафиксировал бычий сигнал по $ETH.
Текущая котировка ETH. Данные разбираемого сигнала зафиксированы в 18:14 UTC+5:
{spot}(ETHUSDT)
Проверка качества отклонила вход. Разберём почему: убедительная цифра на экране ещё не показывает, насколько надёжен сам прогноз. Причина заслуживает отдельного разбора: убедительная цифра на экране ещё не показывает, насколько надёжен сам прогноз.
Я разрабатываю MaBuy как проект рыночной аналитики. Ниже — учебный разбор записанного решения. Это отклонённый сигнал, а не исполненная сделка и не результат paper-позиции.
Что было известно в момент решения
Запись зафиксирована 5 октября 2026 года в 18:14:36 UTC+5. Модели использовали закрытые часовые свечи; последняя закрылась в 18:00.
В журнале сохранились следующие значения:
направление итогового прогноза — вверх;эвристическая оценка сигнала — 81,4%;сырой выход LSTM — около +5,16% в шкале логдоходности;установленный предел допуска для сырого выхода — ±2,50% в той же шкале.
Логдоходность — способ выразить отношение двух цен через логарифм. Здесь она нужна для сравнения выходов модели с пределом проверки. Число +5,16% не является полученной прибылью, доходностью позиции с плечом или обещанием роста ETH.
Почему большая цифра стала причиной отказа
Выход LSTM превышал положительный предел примерно в 2,06 раза. В текущей конфигурации MaBuy это достаточная причина, чтобы не допустить такой прогноз к новому входу.
Предел ±2,50% — настройка нашей проверки качества. Он не означает, что рынок физически не способен пройти больше за час. Превышение говорит, что выход модели находится за пределами диапазона, который мы сейчас допускаем для решений.
В журнале это отмечено кодом PYTORCH_RETURN_SATURATED. Название техническое, но смысл в данном случае простой: сырой прогноз вышел за установленную границу. Сам код не доказывает вычислительное переполнение и не объясняет причину такого выхода модели.
Был и второй отказ: дополнительная статистическая проверка не подтвердила персистентность движения в выбранном окне. Иначе говоря, система не получила необходимого подтверждения устойчивости ряда для этого входа. Это не прогноз разворота и не доказательство, что цена дальше обязательно пойдёт вниз.
А как же оценка 81,4%?
В нашей текущей системе эта оценка эвристическая и не откалибрована по частоте прибыльных сделок.
Поэтому её нельзя читать как «81,4% вероятности заработать». Она также не является винрейтом проекта. Для подобных выводов нужна отдельная проверка на будущих данных и результатах с учтёнными издержками.
Именно поэтому оценка сигнала и допуск по качеству проверяются отдельно. Высокая оценка не отменяет проблему в исходных выходах модели. В этом наблюдении направление осталось бычьим, а проверка качества сохранила решение об отказе. Прогноз и причины отказа записаны для дальнейшего анализа.
Что этот пример пока не доказывает
На момент решения будущий результат ещё не был известен. Поэтому я не называю этот отказ спасённым депозитом или предотвращённым убытком.
Цена могла вырасти после отклонённого сигнала. Тогда возник бы вопрос об упущенной возможности. Она могла снизиться — но один такой эпизод всё равно не подтвердил бы полезность фильтра на дистанции.
Чтобы оценить правило, нужно смотреть серию наблюдений: какие сигналы оно пропускает, какие отклоняет и как меняется результат после комиссий, funding и проскальзывания. При этом условия проверки должны быть зафиксированы до оценки результата.
Мне кажется, именно здесь начинается дисциплина анализа: сначала определить, какие данные заслуживают доверия, затем обсуждать вход и риск. Впечатляющий прогноз может стать поводом проверить модель внимательнее.
Что для вас сложнее: принять убыток в рамках заранее заданного плана или пропустить рост из-за собственных правил?
Учебный разбор собственного проекта. Не является индивидуальной инвестиционной рекомендацией.

#以太坊质押退出队列创2026年新高 When people calculate the returns on ETH staking, they rarely put a price on how long it takes to exit.

Ethereum’s staking exit queue has hit a new high for 2026. As of October 5, around 786,000 ETH were waiting to exit, with a wait of nearly 14 days, followed by withdrawal processing.

This surge is related to preventive exits by MetaMask validators. Lido expects the ETH involved to be gradually restaked, so there isn’t enough evidence to treat the entire queue as ETH poised to be dumped on the market.

But there’s a more consequential question for returns: what if you need the money today?
People holding staking tokens such as stETH can exchange them for ETH on the secondary market. However, the price they get depends on market supply and demand, as well as trading depth.

If many people are rushing to exit and few are willing to buy, they may have to accept a lower price. The wait for protocol redemptions also depends on factors such as available buffer funds, so you can’t simply apply the validators’ 14-day queue time.

Assume an annual yield of 3%. If an urgent exchange costs you 1%, that’s equivalent to losing about four months of yield.

This is an illustrative calculation; it doesn’t mean that stETH is currently trading at a 1% discount.

So the key things to watch next are the price of stETH-to-ETH exchanges, actual redemption times, and slippage on large trades. If these indicators deteriorate significantly, that would provide more direct evidence of liquidity pressure.

Staking yields are presented on an annual basis, while liquidity costs may all come due on the day you urgently need your money.
Putting money you’ll need in the short term into long-term staking for yield creates a maturity mismatch—and that’s more concerning than earning a slightly lower APR.
#以太坊质押退出队列创2026年新高 #ETH

#以太坊质押退出队列创2026年新高 ETH质押这件事，大家算收益的时候，很少给“退出要等多久”标价。

以太坊质押退出队列创2026年新高。10月5日的数据是约78.6万枚ETH排队退出，等待接近14天，后面还涉及提现处理。

这次激增与MetaMask验证者的预防性退出有关。Lido预计相关ETH会逐步重新质押，所以直接把整个队列当成砸盘资金，依据不足。

但这里有个更影响收益的问题：如果你今天就需要用钱，怎么办？
持有stETH这类质押凭证的人，可以在二级市场换回ETH。不过，成交价格取决于市场供需和交易深度。

急着退出的人多、愿意接的人少，就可能要让价。协议赎回的等待时间则还取决于缓冲资金等因素，不能直接套用验证者队列的14天。

假设年收益3%，一次急用钱的兑换损耗了1%，相当于约4个月的收益被吃掉。

这是算账示例，不代表现在stETH已经折价1%。

所以，这个话题后续最值得盯的，是stETH兑换ETH的价格、实际赎回时间，以及大额兑换的滑点。如果这些指标明显恶化，流动性压力才有更直接的证据。

质押收益按年展示，流动性成本可能在你急用钱的那一天集中结算。
把短期要用的钱拿去赚长期质押收益，这个期限错配，比少赚一点APR更值得担心。

Can someone who’s obsessed with crypto trading really go back to being normal?
#ETH 
Honestly, it’s pretty hard. Ying had a follower who once casually tried out futures trading.

He started with 1,500 USDT and turned it into 40,000 USDT in two days. Those few days, he was on top of the world—walking with a spring in his step. He really thought making money was as easy as picking it up off the ground, and even felt$AKE that he’d discovered the “truth” of the market.

What happened next?
He went all in, used heavy leverage, and stubbornly held on through the losses. Before long, his 40,000 USDT had dwindled back down to a few hundred.

But the scariest part wasn’t losing it all. It was that he couldn’t kick the rush.

From then on, he lived like a machine glued to the charts. He skipped meals, went without sleep, and kept his phone in his hand 24/7. He’d say “Never touch futures” every day, but the moment the market twitched, he’d still be the first to jump in and get rekt.

Put simply, the most dangerous thing about futures is that they’re fast.
With leverage of dozens of times, even a small move in the right direction can make your account balance shoot up faster than your heartbeat. It’s way more thrilling than stocks, and more addictive than most things.

A 10% gain or loss in a day is big news in the stock market. But in crypto, moves of dozens of percentage points—or even a doubling—in a single day are nothing unusual.

Once you’ve tasted a big win, your brain will cling to that rush.

A lot of people have the same thought bottled up inside: “Just one more time, and I’ll win it all back.”

But reality tends to slap you in the face. Most people’s accounts are quietly wiped out by the market before they ever get the chance to “turn things around” $US

That’s why, once you get involved with high leverage, it’s so hard to walk away.

It’s not that people are especially greedy. It’s that the speed and thrill can drag you into the abyss so easily.

It just takes many people a while to realize: the more a place feels like a dream, the heavier the price you’ll often pay.

#ETH The one thing small accounts should avoid most: seeing a glimmer of hope and immediately betting everything on it

When people have only a few hundred or a few thousand U in starting capital, they often feel their funds are too limited. They think that to grow quickly, they have to use heavy leverage, go all in, and catch one big move.

But in reality, before their money has a chance to grow, their own trading often knocks them out of the market.

Brother Xia has seen plenty of people make a little money from a few small moves. Their accounts start growing, and their confidence grows along with them. They think they've found the secret to making money, then start going all in to chase hot trends, buying high and selling low.

Then, as soon as they get the direction wrong, one drawdown wipes out all the profits they've built up—and may even eat into their initial capital.

The most important thing when growing a small account isn't betting on a single opportunity. It's making sure you can always stay in the market.

You have to manage your position size. Don't put all your chips on the table from the start. There will always be more opportunities in the market. But if one bad trade leaves you without the capital to take part in the next move, that's the real problem.

Also, don't try to catch every market move. Don't rush in just because others are making money, and don't blindly buy the dip when prices plunge. If you haven't read the trend clearly, assessed the price level, or worked out the risk, it's better to miss out than to jump in recklessly.

One of the most important lessons in trading is learning to accept mistakes.
No one can guarantee that every trade will be right. Cutting your losses promptly when you're wrong is far better than holding a losing position and fantasizing about a rebound. Many people don't lose money because of one mistake; they lose because they refuse to admit it, and end up sinking deeper and deeper.

After making a profit, you also need to know how to protect it. When the market is moving in your favor, you can take profits in stages. Don't always expect to capture the entire move. There's always more money to be made in the market, but once you lose your capital, starting over can be difficult.

Compounding a position has never been about getting rich through luck. It's about repeatedly doing the right things and gradually building up a small edge.

First, keep your capital alive. Then think about growing your returns.

A truly skilled trader isn't someone who catches every opportunity. They're someone who's already prepared before the opportunity arrives.

#ETH 小资金最忌讳的一件事：刚看到希望，就开始拿命去赌

很多人本金只有几百U、几千U的时候，总觉得自己资金太少，想快速做大就必须重仓、梭哈、抓一波大的

但现实往往是，钱还没滚起来，人先被自己的操作搞出局了

侠哥见过不少人，前面靠几次小行情赚了一点，账户开始增长，心态也跟着膨胀，觉得自己已经找到赚钱的方法，然后开始满仓追热点、追涨杀跌

结果一旦方向判断错，一次回撤就把之前积累的利润全部打回去，甚至本金都受到影响

其实小资金想做大，最重要的不是赌一次机会，而是保证自己一直有资格留在市场里

仓位一定要控制，不要一开始就把所有筹码压上。市场机会永远都有，但如果一次操作失误导致没有本金参与下一次行情，那才是真正的问题

还有就是不要什么行情都想抓，别人赚钱的时候别急着冲，看到暴跌也别盲目抄底。趋势没看清，位置没判断好，风险没计算明白，宁愿错过，也不要乱上

交易里最重要的一课，就是接受错误

3x leveraged ETFs target three times the daily return. If the underlying asset rises 5% in a day, the fund gains about 15%; if it falls 5%, the fund loses about 15% (before fees). These products are only suitable for taking intraday directional positions, not for holding long term. In a choppy market, daily rebalancing gradually erodes the fund’s value.

Current prices: BTC at 86,050, up 0.9% over 24 hours, implying an intraday gain of about 2.7% for a leveraged ETF; ETH at 2,716, up 0.5%, implying about 1.5%. Where should the trigger line be? A 5% single-day move in the underlying asset is the threshold. Once it’s reached, the move is amplified threefold. If it isn’t reached, leverage decay takes over, making it poor odds to chase a long position.

Why Are Bitcoin, Ethereum and XRP Prices Up Today?
A weak U.S. jobs report pushed traders to cut their bets on an October Fed rate hike. Last week's PCE inflation data also showed a drop in consumer prices. Bitcoin jumped after that report.
That mix gave crypto some room to rise. Lower rate hike odds usually help risk assets.
What Are the Odds of a Fed Rate Hike in October?
The Fed raised rates by 25 basis points to 3.75% to 4% at its September 16 meeting. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said inflation was "too high" after that.

Fed governor Phillip Jefferson also hinted the Fed might hold rates in October. A week ago, a hike looked likely. A month ago, a cut was on the table at 29.8%. The mood has flipped fast. 
When Are the FOMC Minutes Released, and Will They Move Crypto?
The minutes from the September 15 to 16 meeting come out on Wednesday, October 7. They should show how split the officials were. They may also show how worried the Fed is about inflation and jobs.
Traders will look for a hawkish or dovish tone. Treasury yields, the dollar, and risk appetite can all react. 

There is also a wild card. The U.S. and Iran are reportedly bracing for fresh attacks after new developments over the weekend. News from the Middle East could shake markets fast.
Is the Crypto Market in Fear or Greed Right Now?
The Fear & Greed Index reads 70, which is Greed. That means traders are fairly optimistic.

Are Crypto ETFs Seeing Inflows or Outflows?
Bitcoin spot ETFs took in $241.09 million last week, as of October 2. That follows a much bigger $2.39 billion inflow the week before. Total net inflow now stands at $57.79 billion, and net assets are about $108.89 billion.
Ethereum spot ETFs saw outflows of $37.36 million on October 2. Before that, $55.37 million left on October 1 and $59.8 million on September 30. Cumulative net inflow is $13.80 billion.

This is a view, not a promise. A drop below $80,000 would weaken the setup.

【Institutions are quietly pulling out of ETH, but 99% of people haven’t figured out why】

Bitcoin ETFs have seen net inflows for three consecutive weeks, while Ethereum ETFs recorded $138 million in outflows in a single week.

That number may not look huge, but people in the know understand what it means.

The money isn’t fleeing—it’s changing direction.

Why are institutions voting with their feet? I’ve spoken with a few guys who work in quant finance, and their reasoning is straightforward: ETH staking yields are falling, and there are nearly 1.5 million ETH waiting in the staking queue, with a 25-day wait to get in. That liquidity hit is substantial. By contrast, a BTC ETF is just an ETF: you can sell whenever you want. The last thing institutions want is to have their money locked up.

Put simply, ETH’s problem right now isn’t that the technology is bad; it’s that its financial structure isn’t friendly enough to large investors.

So, is ETH finished? No. It’s down 45% from its all-time high, and historically, this range has been a comfortable zone for long-term investors to build positions. The Fear and Greed Index is holding around 70, suggesting market sentiment is still fairly steady—we’re not at panic levels. The key thing to watch is trading volume. Sentiment has been cautious over the past few days, and until volume picks up, the direction remains unclear.

I’m not saying ETH is no good. I’m saying you need to understand the rationale behind what you’re holding.

If you hold ETH now, are you in it for the staking yield, or because you believe in its ecosystem and applications? If it’s the former, you should recalculate whether the cost of locking up your assets makes sense. If it’s the latter, don’t worry about short-term volatility—keep your eye on real-world usage.

So here’s the question: ETH’s staking mechanism may work well for retail investors, but it’s not flexible enough for institutions. Could that be a structural problem in the long run?

content:
【机构正在悄悄撤离ETH，但99%的人还没看懂】

比特币ETF连续三周净流入，以太坊ETF单周流出1.38亿美元。

这数字看着不大，但懂行的人知道这意味着什么。

资金不是在跑，是在换方向。

为什么机构开始用脚投票？我跟几个做量化的小伙子聊过，他们的逻辑很直接：ETH的质押收益在降，质押队列排了将近150万枚ETH，等25天才能进去，这流动性折损不是一般的大。反观BTC，ETF就是ETF，买了随时能跑，机构最怕的就是锁死。

说白了，ETH现在的问题不是技术不行，是它的金融结构对大资金不够友好。

那ETH是不是完了？不是。这个位置较历史高点跌了45%，历史上这个区间都是长线资金建仓的舒适区。恐惧贪婪指数维持在70附近，说明市场情绪还算稳，没到恐慌的时候。关键看成交量，这几天观望情绪重，没放量之前，方向还不明确。

我不是说ETH不行，我是说你要看清楚自己手里的东西是什么逻辑。

你现在持有ETH，是冲着质押收益去的，还是看好生态应用？如果是前者，现在这个锁仓成本你得重新算算账。如果是后者，那就别管短期波动，盯着真实使用量说话。

所以问题来了——ETH这套质押机制，对散户友好，但对机构不够灵活，长远看这是不是个结构性问题？

CoinGecko在2026年10月5日19时35分（北京时间）发布的当次快照显示，EDEL在该平台过去24小时搜索关注榜中位列第2；同一快照中，其市值排名为第661位。以上是可核实的事实，数据归属CoinGecko，性质为单时点观察。
需要明确几条指标边界：其一，该榜单衡量的是搜索行为带来的关注度，不等于买盘、资金净流入或成交量放大，关注度高并不必然对应交易需求上升；其二，本次为单次快照，缺少前次数据对比，无法判断排名属于上升、回落还是持平，也不宜据此描述热度持续；其三，这是CoinGecko的统计口径，并非币安榜单，两者用户群体与算法不同；其四，现有证据中没有项目公告、上所、合作或安全事件等信息，此次排名对应的驱动原因未知，不应为其补写利好或利空叙事。
另可记录一处事实性落差：搜索榜第2位与市值第661位差距明显。这属于推测层面的观察：小市值资产在搜索端的波动往往先于、且大于交易端的实际变化，但本例是否如此，需要后续数据验证。
待观察事项包括：后续快照中EDEL排名能否保持，还是一次性冲高后回落；成交量与流动性是否与搜索关注度匹配；市值排名是否随之变动；项目方是否发布能解释关注度变化的公告。在上述信息补齐之前，本文仅作事实层面的记录，涉及原因与走向的判断均属推测。

translatedData.title: Short ETH, don’t go long
translatedData.subTitle:
1. Upgrades don’t make the price rise
 
Every time ETH gets an upgrade, everyone expects a rally, but each time they’re disappointed. The positive news has already been priced in, so the announcement itself ends up marking a peak.
 
2. The data is fake
 
Many of those “new users” and “active addresses” on-chain are generated by bots, not real people. It may look lively, but it’s just a mirage.
 
3. Deflation is gone
 
ETH used to be considered valuable because its supply was expected to keep shrinking. Now the amount burned has plunged, and the supply is growing again. Scarcity creates value—but if it’s no longer scarce, why should it be valuable?
 
4. Whales are short
 
Whales with positions worth millions of dollars are more heavily short than long. Retail investors, meanwhile, are rushing to go long—and following the crowd often means losing money.

title: ETH's Exit Queue Jumps 392% to 850,736 ETH, the Longest Wait All Year
subTitle:
Over 60% of it traces back to MetaMask's precautionary validator exits. Here's what a 14.77-day wait actually means for the market.

🚀 In late September, Ethereum's validator exit queue sat around 100,000 ETH, unremarkable, business as usual. By October 2, it had climbed to nearly 850,736 ETH, a 392% jump that pushed the estimated wait time to 14.77 days, the longest queue Ethereum has seen all year.
That's a lot of people lining up to stop staking at once. But the reason behind it isn't what you might assume.
🔐 Most of this isn't holders fleeing a falling price. It's a security response.
Roughly 523,000 ETH of that total, over 60% of the entire queue, traces directly back to MetaMask Staking. On September 30, MetaMask disclosed that part of its infrastructure had been compromised. The company said about 0.36 ETH in block rewards across 18 blocks was briefly transferred, while user wallets and sensitive data weren't affected. In response, MetaMask arranged the exit of nearly 17,000 validators, much of it tied to Lido operations, as a precaution. That process is expected to finish by October 7.
🧮 So what's the other roughly 40%?
That portion doesn't have a single clean explanation, and it's worth being honest about that rather than forcing a tidy narrative onto it. Litecoin mining pool founder Jiang Zhuoer offered one read, suggesting the jump reflects some holders using current prices to lock in profits. That's a plausible interpretation, not a confirmed one. ETH traded in a narrow range between $2,686 and $2,725 from September 30 to October 2, a level some long-term holders may view as a reasonable exit point, but the queue data itself doesn't tell you why any individual validator chose to leave.
📊 Here's the context that keeps this from being alarming on its own.
Ethereum still has about 43.6 million ETH staked across roughly 878,000 active validators. Even at its peak, this exit queue represents only about 2% of total staked supply. A 14.77-day wait sounds dramatic as a standalone number, but set against the full staking base, it's a meaningful spike, not a system under strain.
🧠 Why does the "security response vs. profit-taking" distinction actually matter?
Because the two scenarios tell you very different things about market sentiment. A queue driven mostly by one company's defensive, one-time validator migration is a contained, explainable event with a known end date, October 7. A queue driven mostly by holders deciding the price is high enough to cash out would be a genuine sentiment signal worth tracking closely. Right now, the data suggests it's mostly the former, with some of the latter mixed in, not the reverse.
✅ What this means for you
If you're staking ETH, this is a useful moment to understand what you're actually watching. Once MetaMask's precautionary exits complete around October 7, the queue should shrink meaningfully unless a fresh wave of unrelated exits appears, that's the clean signal to check for afterward.
If you're evaluating ETH's price action, don't read this queue spike as a standalone bearish signal. The dominant driver is a security-related migration, not a broad loss of staking conviction. Watch whether the queue stays elevated after October 7, that would be the real tell that profit-taking is playing a bigger role than currently visible.
If you're tracking MetaMask's broader situation, this is worth following alongside anything else the company discloses about the incident's scope. A 0.36 ETH loss across 18 blocks is small in isolation, but a 17,000-validator precautionary exit is a significant operational response, worth understanding fully once more details emerge.
🟢 What would confirm this is mostly a contained event
The queue drops substantially once MetaMask's exits finish around October 7, no comparable new wave of exits appears afterward, and this settles as a one-time security response rather than an ongoing trend.
🔴 What would suggest broader profit-taking is the real story
The queue stays elevated even after MetaMask's exits complete, more validators continue exiting at a similar pace, and ETH price weakness follows as unstaked ETH becomes liquid and some portion reaches exchanges.
👀 Three things to watch
1️⃣ The queue after October 7
Does it shrink meaningfully once MetaMask's precautionary exits finish, confirming this was mostly a one-time event?
2️⃣ MetaMask's further disclosures
Does the company share more detail about the scope and cause of the infrastructure compromise, or does September 30's statement stay the full picture?
3️⃣ ETH price behavior as exits complete
Does price hold steady as the 523,000 MetaMask-linked ETH clears the queue, or does some of it translate into visible sell pressure?
💡 The key takeaway
A 392% jump in Ethereum's exit queue sounds like a major sentiment shift. Most of it, over 60%, traces to one company's defensive response to a security incident, with a known timeline and a modest confirmed impact.
The real question is whether the queue returns to normal once MetaMask's exits finish on schedule, or whether the remaining, less-explained portion of the spike turns out to be the start of a broader trend.
That is the part worth watching.

This time, it’s not that nobody wants to stake Ethereum. Instead, a large amount of ETH has suddenly started queuing up to “get off the train”!
In just 3 days, the amount of ETH waiting to exit staking surged from about 166,000 to 851,000—more than a fivefold increase. So far, around 786,000 ETH are still queued to exit, worth over $2 billion, with an estimated wait time of nearly 14 days.

🔥 Why are so many people suddenly looking to exit?
The main reason points to MetaMask. On September 30, MetaMask disclosed a security incident and suspended services for some affected validators. After that, to reduce potential risks, the validators involved began exiting Ethereum staking. This directly overwhelmed the ETH exit queue.
Some researchers estimate that these precautionary exits may involve around 17,000 validators, representing approximately 523,000 ETH, though MetaMask has not confirmed this specific figure.

So, this wave of ETH exits shouldn’t be simply interpreted as:
“People have lost faith in Ethereum and are frantically selling their coins.”
⚠️ More accurately, this large-scale exit is mainly related to validators withdrawing after the MetaMask security incident.
And there’s another very important detail—
This ETH doesn’t all enter the market immediately after exiting. To prevent validators from entering and exiting en masse at the same time, Ethereum limits how much ETH can enter or exit each day.

At present, the network can process only about 57,600 ETH per day.
That means if hundreds of thousands or even millions of ETH suddenly want to exit, they have to queue.
📌 The exit queue has now reached a record high of 2,026.
But don’t rush to interpret this as “$2 billion worth of ETH is about to be dumped.”

Because exiting staking ≠ selling immediately.
The ETH still has to go through the withdrawal process before it can actually return to holders’ wallets. Lido estimates that for the affected validators, exiting, withdrawing, and re-entering the staking system could take around 45 days in total.

Markets never go up without ever coming down. I believe that after a period of gains, Ethereum is quite likely to see a substantial correction. But what really matters to me isn’t “how far it will fall”; it’s whether I can seize the opportunity to accumulate gradually when market sentiment sinks back into fear.

If Ethereum does enter a sharp correction, I won’t put all my capital in at once. No one can know exactly where the bottom is, and even if you get the long-term direction right, you could still face unrealized losses of 20%, 30%, or even more after buying the dip. So my strategy would be to divide my capital into several portions and build a position gradually as the price falls. The further it drops, the more I’d consider increasing the amount I invest, rather than using up all my ammunition as soon as the first big decline hits.

Major rallies often don’t begin when everyone is optimistic. When the market is full of optimism and people everywhere are talking about new highs, prices have usually already risen substantially. It may be more worthwhile to reassess the risk-reward ratio during a deep correction—when leveraged positions are being liquidated, retail investors are losing confidence, and voices are emerging again asking, “Is Ethereum finished?”

So I’m not simply waiting for a price drop, but for a phase in which I can accumulate again. If the fundamentals and long-term thesis remain intact, a sharp price correction may offer a better average entry price. My goal isn’t to call the exact bottom, but to gradually build a position in the market’s most pessimistic phase—one that is cheap enough while still allowing me to withstand the volatility.

What a bull market really tests isn’t who dares to chase higher prices, but who still has the capital, discipline, and patience to stick to their plan when the market corrects and their portfolio is deep in the red. 一、以太坊市场深度分析：两千七百美元区间的蓄势待发

截至二零二六年十月五日上午，以太坊报价两千七百二十二点九四美元，过去二十四小时上涨百分之零点七三。价格在触及两千七百三十四点五五美元的日内高点后小幅回落，目前在两千七百美元上方窄幅整理。与比特币相比，以太坊的涨幅略显温和，但技术面呈现出更为积极的中期信号。

二、技术指标全面解读

从均线系统来看，七周期均线报两千七百一十六点五九美元，二十五周期均线报两千七百一十点七六美元，九十九周期均线报两千六百九十九点九零美元。三条均线呈现标准的多头排列，且间距适中，表明趋势运行健康。价格始终运行在所有均线上方，短期支撑位位于两千七百一十美元附近。

布林带指标显示，上轨位于两千七百三十七点七三美元，中轨位于两千七百一十三点五九美元，下轨位于两千六百八十九点四五美元。当前价格在中轨与上轨之间运行，接近通道上沿但未突破。布林带开口平稳，波动率处于正常水平。

MACD指标方面，DIF线报五点九四，DEA线报六点三六，柱状线为负零点四二。MACD柱状线刚刚由正转负，但绝对值较小，显示空头力量有限。此前柱状线曾短暂转正至零点一四，表明多头曾尝试发力但未能持续。整体来看，MACD处于零轴上方的弱势调整状态，尚不构成趋势反转信号。

RSI指标中，六周期RSI报四十八点六七，十二周期RSI报五十点六五，二十四周期RSI报五十四点四三。三条RSI线均处于五十附近的中性区域，既没有超买也没有超卖，表明市场处于均衡状态，等待新的催化剂打破平衡。

KDJ随机指标中，K线报五十五点七零，D线报五十五点一七，J线报五十六点七六。三线粘合在五十上方，方向不明确，暗示短期可能维持震荡格局。威廉指标报负五十点五八，处于中性区域。

综合指标方面，十五个因子中有十个发出做多信号，四个发出做空信号，一个中性。综合指标信号方向为做多，历史胜率高达百分之九十点九一。这一数据在所有指标中表现极为突出，表明以太坊的中期上涨概率显著高于比特币。

三、市场情绪与基本面分析

以太坊近期最大的利好来自监管层面的突破。美国证券交易委员会批准了首只三倍杠杆以太坊期货ETF，这是继三倍比特币期货ETF之后的又一重要里程碑。该产品的获批不仅扩大了机构投资者对以太坊的杠杆敞口选择，更释放出监管层对加密金融衍生品持续开放的积极信号。SEC同时批准了涵盖黄金、白银、原油等大宗商品的杠杆ETF，表明整体监管环境趋于宽松。

从链上数据来看，以太坊质押需求依然旺盛，约有十四万九千枚ETH处于质押入场队列中，反映出长期持有者对网络价值的信心。然而，验证者退出队列也扩大至约八十五万一千枚ETH，等待时间约十四天。这一退出潮主要受安全因素驱动，短期内可能形成一定的抛售压力。

资金流向方面，现货以太坊ETF上周录得一亿三千八百万美元的净流出，与比特币ETF的持续流入形成鲜明对比。这表明机构投资者在BTC和ETH之间的配置偏好出现分化，资金更倾向于流向比特币。然而，大户买入数据显示出现了两笔大额资金流入，分别为两千八百四十万美元和一千五百八十万美元，有效吸收了卖盘压力，推动价格触及日内高点。

鲸鱼动向同样值得关注。多个休眠钱包和生态内部人士近期向中心化交易所转入超过一万七千枚ETH，增加了潜在的抛售风险。但从另一个角度看，这些转账也可能用于质押或流动性提供，并非全部意味着卖出。

从生态发展来看，BNB Chain和Solana上的代币化股票规模分别达到十一亿美元和四十四亿美元的月交易量，以太坊在这一领域面临竞争压力。但以太坊依然是DeFi和智能合约的核心平台，其网络效应和开发者生态的优势短期内难以被替代。今晚即将发布的Binance Intelligence AI产品也引发了市场的广泛关注，BNB已攀升至八百一十美元的高位。

四、热门代币速览

GTC当前报价零点二二零二九美元，二十四小时涨幅百分之七十八点九二。Gitcoin社区提出的品牌重塑方案引发市场热烈讨论，代币价格单日暴涨但技术指标严重超买。

MOVR当前报价二点三零五美元，二十四小时涨幅百分之二十三九二。Moonriver作为Moonbeam的姐妹网络，近期生态合作增多推动代币走强。

SCR当前报价零点零二九六七美元，二十四小时涨幅百分之十七点八三。Scroll作为以太坊Layer2解决方案，持续获得开发者关注。

五、总结与展望

以太坊当前处于窄幅震荡阶段，短期技术指标显示方向不明，但中期综合指标的做多胜率高达百分之九十以上，为所有主流资产中最高。三倍杠杆ETF的获批、质押需求的持续增长以及大户资金的积极介入，都为价格提供了有力支撑。投资者需关注验证者退出潮的演变以及ETF资金流向的变化，在两千七百美元支撑位上方保持适度乐观，同时警惕两千七百四十美元阻力位的突破情况。

Ethereum’s validator exit queue jumped 392% since the start of October, reaching roughly 851,000 ETH at its peak.

Why did I stop copy trading? The risk is high. I did make money, but really, I need to be in control myself. Maybe I’m better off not copying trades. I’m often afraid to enter at certain price levels, so perhaps other people’s high leverage and position sizing can make up for my shortcomings. After a week of copy trading, I realized there were quite a few problems. First, when a trade went wrong, the trader didn’t admit it in time. It could have been closed at breakeven, but instead it was allowed to turn into a stop-loss. I often manually managed the stop loss and take profit, and even the timing of entries. I’d only let the signal provider place a trade when I thought it was a good entry, and in the end, I always came out profitable. But today I noticed the signal provider’s position was already down to half size. They do trade very quickly, but the drawdown was also huge. Thankfully, I made a decisive choice at the time: I lost 80 USDT and stopped copy trading immediately. The people copying trades today weren’t so lucky; most of them suffered heavy losses. So I think it’s fine to experiment with copy trading, but never hand over all your capital to someone else, no matter how skilled they are. When there are profits, they take a cut; when there are losses, there’s no compensation.

I was still pretty nervous today. The price was pressing against the trendline, and I didn’t dare enter a trade. I only put in 100 USDT, and it turned out exactly as expected. I took a small profit and got out.

title: ETH验证者退出量突然暴增392%，但市场却没怎么跌。
subTitle:
10月初，以太坊验证者退出队列一度接近 85万枚ETH，约占全网质押量的2%，按目前速度需要排队约 14.77天。

这次最大的原因，是 MetaMask Staking 9月30日披露基础设施遭入侵，随后作为预防措施安排约 1.7万个验证者退出，涉及约52.3万枚ETH，其中不少与 Lido 运营商有关。

但这里有个容易被误解的地方：

验证者退出 ≠ ETH马上砸盘。

退出本身需要排队，而且整个过程被拉长到十几天。即使有人退出后卖出，卖压也是慢慢释放，不会一下子砸到市场上。

所以这几天ETH依然在 2686～2725美元附近运行，并没有出现与85万ETH退出规模相匹配的剧烈下跌。

另外，也不能把所有退出都理解成“恐慌跑路”。部分持有人可能只是觉得当前价格不错，选择先落袋为安。

MetaMask这批退出预计 10月7日前后完成，届时退出队列有望明显下降。

真正值得关注的，反而是另一件事：

单个大型质押基础设施的一次安全事件，就能影响几十万枚ETH的退出节奏。

这提醒我们，ETH质押规模越来越大之后，质押池、节点运营商和基础设施的集中度，本身也是需要关注的风险。

目前全网仍有约 4360万枚ETH处于质押状态。

所以这次更像是一次集中退出事件，暂时还没看到它演变成全网级别的ETH抛售。
#ETH

translatedData.title: ETH validator exits suddenly surged 392%, but the market barely fell.
translatedData.subTitle:
In early October, the Ethereum validator exit queue briefly approached 850,000 ETH, about 2% of the network’s total staked ETH. At the current rate, validators would need to wait around 14.77 days to exit.

The main reason was that MetaMask Staking disclosed on September 30 that its infrastructure had been compromised. It then arranged for around 17,000 validators to exit as a precaution, involving about 523,000 ETH, much of it linked to Lido operators.

But there’s an easy point to misunderstand here:

Validator exits ≠ ETH being dumped immediately.

Exits have to wait in a queue, and the whole process stretches over more than ten days. Even if some validators sell after exiting, the selling pressure is released gradually rather than hitting the market all at once.

🚀 Smart Money Concepts — From Zero to Advanced
Day 4: Supply & Demand Zones
 
Stop drawing support and resistance as single lines only.
Price often doesn’t react to an exact line; it reacts within broader zones of liquidity and order flow. 🧵👇
 $BTC 
{spot}(BTCUSDT)

In institutional market structure, liquidity can cluster around obvious support and resistance levels. That’s why traders using smart-money-style analysis often mark Supply Zones and Demand Zones as boxes.
 
1. The Displacement Rule — Potential Footprint of Strong Participation
 $ETH 
{spot}(ETHUSDT)
Demand Zone:
The last bearish candle or consolidation area on the chart from which price made a strong bullish displacement. If the move broke structure or left an imbalance/FVG, the zone may be more relevant.
 $SOL 
{spot}(SOLUSDT)

Supply Zone
The last bullish candle or consolidation area from which price moved aggressively downward. Strong bearish displacement and a market-structure shift can make this zone more meaningful.
 
 
Important: A zone isn’t valid just because price moved away from it—context and confirmation matter.
 
 
2. Volume Validation vs. Low-Conviction Moves
 
To assess a zone’s quality, consider:
 
• Was there strong momentum in the move away from the zone?
• Did price break structure?
• Was an imbalance/FVG created?
• Was volume strong relative to the surrounding activity?
• Has the zone already been tested multiple times?
 
Strong displacement + structure break + imbalance + healthy volume can create stronger confluence. However, a low-volume breakout or weak follow-through could also be a failed move or a liquidity sweep.
 
💡 Core Takeaway
Instead of blindly reacting to a single support/resistance line, mark as boxes the areas from which price created strong displacement, an imbalance/FVG, or a structure shift. Wait for confirmation when the zone is retested, and define your invalidation risk in advance.

title: BTC没站稳8.7万，先查这单会被谁吃掉成本
subTitle:
BTC没站稳8.7万，先查这单会被谁吃掉成本

今天盘面最容易误导人的地方，不是 BTC 一度冲到 8.7 万美元附近，也不是回到 8.6 万附近后大家又开始讨论顺势交易，而是很多人会把“价格回来了”误读成“成交环境也回来了”。

这两件事不是一回事。

价格是一条线，成交是一整套环境。尤其在冲高回落后的几个小时里，盘口会变得很微妙：看起来买卖盘还在，真正能承接的深度却不一定厚；报价还在刷新，但报价层之间可能已经拉开；同一个交易对，不同路径看到的价差、撮合速度、手续费结构、触发规则都可能不一样。

所以这时候下单，最怕的不是你没看懂 K 线，而是你只看懂了 K 线。

比如你准备做一笔 20,000 USDT 名义规模的合约单，图表上看到的是同一个 BTC 价格，实际成交时面对的却可能是几套完全不同的订单环境。一边报价看着紧，但深度只集中在第一层；一边价差略宽，但后面的承接更完整；还有一些路径在行情快速变化时，预估价格和真实成交之间会出现明显漂移。

这就是为什么冲高回落后的交易，很多人复盘时会觉得奇怪：方向大体没错，进场位置也不是离谱，可最后盈亏就是比想象中难看。问题可能不在判断本身，而在那一单穿过了什么样的报价层。

合约交易里，成本不是只有手续费。价差是成本，滑点是成本，深度断层是成本，触发条件差异也是成本。更隐蔽的是规则设计：同样是价格波动，有的路径先让你成交，有的路径先让你排队；有的路径预估损耗更明显，有的路径在快行情里会把你的风险缓冲压得很薄。

行情越热，这些差异越不应该被省略。

因为热盘面会放大两个动作：一是追价，二是撤单。追价让订单更急，撤单让盘口更空。你在图上看到的是一分钟内的上影线和回落，真实下单时遇到的可能是某几秒钟里报价层突然变薄、可成交数量突然变少、预估成本突然抬高。

这也是我现在越来越不喜欢只问“BTC能不能继续上”的原因。这个问题当然重要，但它只回答方向，不回答执行。真正决定这一单舒不舒服的，是你在下单前有没有看过三件事：

第一，当前价差有没有明显变宽。价差变宽时，很多看似接近现价的订单，其实从按下按钮那一刻就已经带着成本。

第二，深度是不是集中在表层。如果只有第一层好看，后面承接稀薄，稍微大一点的单子就可能把平均成交价推歪。

第三，不同路径的触发和成交规则是否一致。尤其在冲高回落后，订单环境变化比方向讨论更快，规则差异会直接影响真实结果。

很多交易者亏得不服气，是因为复盘时只看图表，不看订单环境。可市场不会按图表给你成交，它只按当时可用的流动性、报价层和规则给你结果。

所以我的判断很简单：BTC 冲到 8.7 万附近又回落以后，真正该做的不是急着证明自己看对方向，而是先问这一单会从哪里被吃成本。看图决定要不要交易，看订单环境决定这单值不值得现在交易。

这也是 PerpEX 这类执行比较视角存在的意义：不是替你判断涨跌，而是把不同路径的价差、深度、费用和成交偏差先放到桌面上。先选资产，再比较订单环境，最后再决定这一单往哪走。

在流动性越来越分散的市场里，少一次盲下单，往往比多看十根 K 线更值钱。

translatedData.subTitle:
BTC fails to hold $87,000—first check who will absorb the costs of this trade

The most misleading thing about today's market isn't that BTC briefly surged to around $87,000, or that people started talking about trend-following trades again after it returned to around $86,000. It's that many people will mistake “the price is back” for “the trading conditions are back.”

These two things are not the same.

Price is one thing; execution is shaped by an entire set of conditions. This is especially true in the hours after a sharp rise and pullback, when the order book can become quite subtle: buy and sell orders may still appear to be there, but the depth available to absorb trades may not be very strong; quotes may keep updating, while the gaps between price levels widen. Even for the same trading pair, spreads, execution speed, fee structures, and trigger rules can all differ depending on the route used.

Treat trading coins like a job—clock in and clock out every day on time. Don’t mess around with tricks.

In the first few years of trading coins, like many others, I used to stay up late watching the charts, chasing pumps and dumping, and I lost so badly I couldn’t even sleep. Later, I gritted my teeth and stuck to one clumsy method—steady profits.

Here are some proven recommendations for beginners. They’re all experiences I paid for with real money loss:

⸻ 1. Don’t place trades until after 9 PM. During the day, the news gets too chaotic—fake good news and fake bad news fly everywhere. The market jumps up and down like it’s possessed, making it easy to be tricked into entering. I usually wait until after 9 PM to trade. That’s when the news is basically stable, and the candlesticks are cleaner, with clearer direction.
⸻ 2. When you make a profit, take it off the table right away. Don’t always think about doubling! For example, if you made 1000 USDT today, I suggest withdrawing 300 USDT to your bank card through y, and then continue with the rest. I’ve seen too many people who “made three times” and still wanted five times—then one pullback wiped it all out.
⸻ 3. Read indicators, not your feelings. Don’t trade based on gut instinct—that’s just blind guessing. Install TradingView on your phone, and check these indicators before you enter:
• MACD: Is there a golden cross or a dead cross?
• RSI: Is it overbought or oversold?
• Bollinger Bands: Is there a squeeze or a breakout?
If at least two of the three indicators give consistent signals, then consider entering #ETH .
⸻ 4. Stop-loss must be flexible. When you can monitor the market, once you’re in profit, manually move your stop-loss up. For example, if your entry price is 1000 and it rises to 1100, move the stop-loss to 1050 to lock in profit.
But if you need to go out and can’t watch the market, you must set a hard stop-loss of 3% to prevent a sudden crash from wiping you out in one go.
⸻ 5. Take planned withdrawals when you’ve earned money. The money you don’t withdraw is just number games!
⸻ 6. There’s a trick to reading candlesticks.
• For short-term trades: look at the 1-hour chart—if there are two consecutive bullish candles, you can consider going long.
If the market is moving sideways without changing, switch to the 4-hour chart and look for support. Consider entering when price drops near the support level.
⸻ 7. Don’t step into these traps! Don’t go all-in on high leverage. Don’t trade unknown altcoins you don’t understand—you’re easy prey for a liquidation trap.
• No more than 3 trades per day. Too many will make you lose control.
• Absolutely never borrow money to trade coins!
Trading coins isn’t gambling. Treat it like a job: clock in and clock out, shut down when it’s time, eat when you should eat, and sleep when you should sleep. You’ll find the money is actually more stable.#TAKE

Ethereum exits the queue and then drops again, but the hot榜 “jump-up of 392%” is not a reading that is still happening right now. This figure has no attached baseline or statistical window, so it cannot be directly inferred as a new wave of exits.

What’s added this time is a subsequent snapshot from the same page. At 09:36 Beijing time on October 5, the Validator Queue (the page states the data is from beaconcha.in) shows 797,123 ETH, with an estimated wait of 13 days 20 hours; at 14:33 the page shows 786,275 ETH, down by 10,848 ETH (about 1.36%), and the wait estimate shortens to 13 days 16 hours. The page also notes that the data is delayed by 116 minutes relative to the time of reading, so it is not the on-chain instantaneous value at 14:33.

Using the 804,419 ETH recorded at 05:40 as an earlier reference, the page values total a decline of 18,144 ETH (about 2.25%). However, the refresh time gaps between observations are not consistent; this is only a comparison of snapshots presented by the data provider, and it does not mean the queue decreases at the same rate every hour. The processing rate listed on the current page is 256 ETH/epoch; the ETA for withdrawal will change as the queue and processing capacity change, so it cannot be treated as a determined withdrawal date.

The second boundary is that “exit” does not equal “withdrawal already received.” According to Ethereum’s official explanation, validators first complete the exit process and only then enter a withdrawable state; the funds still have to wait for the network to sweep them up. The page’s 7.5-day sweep delay is also only the current estimate. Queued ETH cannot be directly treated as funds already received, and it certainly cannot be equated with spot sell pressure.

To recalculate the hot榜’s 392%, you would need its denominator, start/end time period, and the queue definition being used; the page does not provide this information. Therefore, this article only discusses the subsequent changes in the absolute queued amount. Next, you need to see whether the next refresh from the same data source continues the decline, and to observe the progress of actual exits versus the sweeping of withdrawals. These snapshots alone also cannot explain the ETH price on their own. #ETH
At the network level, it also does not show which operator the holdings belong to, or the actual amount that has already been completed for withdrawal; that requires disclosures from the project team and additional verification using on-chain records.

The SEC Just Approved Something That Didn't Exist a Year Ago: 3x Leveraged Bitcoin ETFs

Most people think of ETFs as the "safe" way to get crypto exposure. This one flips that completely.

The SEC approved a Cboe BZX rule change on Friday allowing six triple-leveraged exchange-traded products from Volatility Shares to list — covering Bitcoin, Ethereum, gold, silver, crude oil, and natural gas.

Here's what "3x leveraged" actually means in practice: if $BTC moves up 5% in a day, the fund targets roughly 15% gain. If it drops 5%, you're looking at roughly 15% loss, in a single session, inside a regular brokerage account.

Important detail most headlines skip: these products use futures contracts, not direct Bitcoin or Ethereum holdings. That adds another layer — futures roll costs and tracking error — on top of the leverage itself.

Timing context: this lands the same week as the SEC's broader custody rule proposals, and approval doesn't mean trading starts immediately — these still need to actually launch on the exchange.

The bigger picture: regulators spent years being cautious about even basic spot $BTC  ETFs. Now leveraged crypto products are clearing hurdles at a pace that would've seemed unthinkable two years ago.

Daily leveraged products are built for short-term trading, not holding — the math compounds against you over time even if the underlying asset eventually recovers. Does easier access to this kind of product help retail investors, or does it mostly just create more ways to get liquidated fast? 👇

📰 Why did Sam Altman warn about the “religionization” of AI? This could affect crypto more than regulation

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has publicly warned that giving AI a religious status is a dangerous idea. This mainly has to do with how AI should be governed—how to build trust—and how to attract investment. Altman’s point is: don’t mythologize AI, and be careful not to go off the rails. This could have a significant impact on the crypto community, since many people see AI and crypto as the big future direction.

Why is this news important?
Why did Altman say this? The core reason is that AI’s moral standing hasn’t been settled yet. If AI is treated like a religion, it could face regulatory resistance the way crypto did in its early days. For example, in some countries today, cryptocurrencies are heavily regulated, partly due to concerns that they could disrupt traditional finance or raise moral issues. Once AI is mythologized, governments may become even more cautious—fearing AI will take control of humans. This would influence the direction of regulation—regulators would be more afraid of AI running out of control; affect investment strategies—investors might feel it’s too far-fetched to invest; and affect public trust—religionization could lead people to question AI’s uncontrollability. Is there a connection to recent events? For instance, Biden recently proposed legislation to regulate AI, concerned about AI-related chaos. Altman’s warning is essentially a reminder not to go to extremes.

Market impact
For BTC and ETH, short-term sentiment could be affected, but the medium- to long-term trend may not change. Why? Because the fundamental logic behind AI and crypto is still technology-driven. If people think AI is being mythologized, in the short run they might see it as “hot,” which could actually stimulate crypto investment. But in the long run, if AI truly becomes “religionized” and triggers tighter regulation, cryptocurrencies (especially those that can be tied to AI concepts—e.g., certain Layer 1/DAO tokens) may be affected. Similar historical events? Not exactly the same, but early religious-style hype around Bitcoin and Ripple also led to increased regulation. So AI religionization is a double-edged sword: it could fuel speculation in the short term, but limit things in the long term.

Trading approach
Altman’s warning is more like a sentiment indicator rather than a direct buy/sell signal. This suggests that the risk of AI-themed altcoins topping out in the near term may increase. However, the overall direction for BTC and ETH is still likely bullish, because AI remains a future trend. A key level to watch is BTC at $82K. In simple terms: the warning about AI religionization is a potential risk point, but the broader crypto outlook remains positive.

Hold on, brothers. The roc rises with the wind in one day and soars ninety thousand miles. Along the way I lost money, got rich, lost money again, and got back up again. I’ve stepped into countless traps, and I’ve also developed my indestructible “Little Strong” personality. I’ve been trading crypto for 12 years, and from losing 8 million at the peak to living freely with no pressure, I’ve summed up 5 “unspoken rules of the crypto world” #ETH 

First, let me introduce myself:

I’m an “old bagholder” who has been grinding in the crypto world for 12 years—no, now I should probably count as a free man who has “turned the tables and sung the song of the liberated peasant.”

Back then I entered with 8,000 yuan, got impulsive and went all-in on altcoins, and at the worst point I lost 8 million...
When I fell so low that I started doubting life, I even considered selling tea eggs. But the tea egg vendor told me: “You should keep trading crypto, don’t steal my job.”
Later, after surviving bull and bear markets and riding through countless crashes, I finally summed up a set of crypto rules that can keep you from getting slaughtered—and occasionally let you do the slaughtering.

1. The market is like romance—don’t go against it
When prices fall, someone always shouts, “Buy the dip, buy the dip!”... Don’t listen; that’s called baiting buyers.
When prices rise, a pullback happens and people start yelling, “It’s over, it’s going to crash!”... Actually, that’s the golden pit.
The market has its rhythm; go with it, don’t sing the opposite tune.

2. Get hyped when you see a price surge? You’re probably just asking to be cleanly and beautifully cut down
Don’t touch a coin that has surged 3x in the short term.
If it stalls at high levels, it will most likely plunge afterward; if you rush in, you’re just helping others break even.

3. MACD is an old friend—entries and exits all depend on it
No need to understand candlesticks in detail; learning MACD is enough:
Entry: DIF and DEA form a golden cross below the zero axis, then break above the zero axis—like a dog suddenly charging out of a mud pit, it might turn into a dark horse.
Reduce position: MACD forms a death cross above the zero axis and starts moving down—run!
MACD looks like a science experiment, but it’s actually a lifesaving candlestick tool.

4. Averaging down is for emotional traders; adding to winners is for professionals
Averaging down on a losing position: you’re emotional. The market falls and you fall even more; it never ends.
Adding to a winning position: this is trend-following thinking. Moving forward with the winners is the only way not to get lost.
